advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether `_improving`/`agreement` should also exclude errored-BASELINE pairs (guard `not a.errored`) to keep criterion (b)'s errored-pair exclusion consistent, and add a test for an errored baseline vs a gold-matching candidate.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/parity.py:132: `def _improving(a: ItemRecord, b: ItemRecord) -> bool:` — guards `not b.errored` only, not `a.errored`

src/rebar/llm/parity.py:140: `agreement = _rate(pairs, lambda p: p[0].decision == p[1].decision or _improving(*p))` — applied over all `pairs`, including errored ones, unlike `live_gold` used for the flip counts (parity.py:151-155)

Docstring/comment at parity.py:128-131 states the errored side's 'synthetic decision earns nothing' and errored pairs are excluded from criterion (b), but the agreement metric now grants forgiveness to an errored-baseline pair

tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py:141 `test_errored_candidate_matching_gold_earns_no_forgiveness` only exercises an errored CANDIDATE (v2), not an errored baseline (v1) — the errored-baseline-forgiven-in-agreement path is untested (ABSENCE of coverage)
advisory.finding: The gold-aware agreement forgiveness applies `_improving` over ALL pairs but only guards `not b.errored` (candidate), not `a.errored` (baseline). So a gold pair where the BASELINE errored and the candidate is a live verdict matching gold with a differing decision now counts as AGREEMENT (was a disagreement before this change), inflating `verdict_agreement` for a pair that criterion (b) documents as excluded because 'criterion (d) already owns runtime errors'.
scenarios: A live parity run where the baseline (v1) times out on a gold item while the candidate (v2) returns the gold-correct decision: agreement is credited full marks for that pair, diverging from the flip counts and the documented errored-pair exclusion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either add `not a.errored` to `_improving`, or compute `agreement` over the errored-excluded live pairs consistently with `live_gold`, and add a test covering an errored baseline (v1) against a gold-matching live candidate (v2).

evidence: tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:405 asserts `report.metrics["decision_flips"] == block["metrics"]["decision_flips"]` but no analogous assertion for `gold_improving_flips`
provider_parity_results.json:61 records `"gold_improving_flips": 2` (frontier) and the standard slot records `1` — the values that flip both slots to `"passed": true`
src/rebar/llm/parity.py:197 adds `gold_improving_flips` to metrics as the new, gating-relevant reclassification signal
ABSENCE: a stale or hand-edited committed `gold_improving_flips` value would recompute differently yet pass this test, since the re-score only compares decision_flips/n_gold/passed/gating_failures
advisory.finding: The offline re-score regression guard for the changed provider_parity_results.json asserts the recomputed decision_flips/n_gold/passed/gating_failures match the committed block but never asserts the recomputed gold_improving_flips equals the committed value — leaving the new headline metric this change introduces unguarded in the recorded artifact.
scenarios: The committed JSON's gold_improving_flips is edited or drifts out of sync with the records (e.g. a future re-record with a scoring change) — the re-score test stays green despite the recorded headline metric being wrong.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert report.metrics["gold_improving_flips"] == block["metrics"]["gold_improving_flips"]` alongside the existing decision_flips assertion at test_provider_parity.py:405.
